question: The 9th Amendment Act, 1960, made adjustments to the Indian territory due to an agreement with which country? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: China
Nepal
Pakistan
Bangladesh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pakistan

Explanation:
The 9th Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution was enacted in 1960 to implement an agreement between India and Pakistan regarding the exchange of certain territories. This agreement, often referred to as the Nehru-Noon Minto Agreement or the Pakistan Border Agreement, aimed to resolve border disputes along the western frontier. Under the pact, India ceded some territories to Pakistan in exchange for others, primarily concerning the Berubari region and Hussainiwala Headworks. The amendment made necessary changes to the First and Fourth Schedules of the Constitution to give effect to the territorial adjustments.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was the 9th Amendment Act of India passed? → 1960
☛ With which country was the territorial adjustment made through the 9th Amendment? → Pakistan
☛ The Nehru-Noon Minto Agreement is related to which border? → India-Pakistan border
☛ Which region is associated with the 9th Amendment? → Berubari
☛ Which schedules were amended by the 9th Amendment? → First and Fourth Schedules

question: Under which Schedule of the Indian Constitution are the provisions for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes provided? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Seventh Schedule
Eighth Schedule
Fourth Schedule
Fifth Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fifth Schedule

Explanation:
The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains provisions for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. It applies to states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. Key provisions include the declaration of Scheduled Areas, establishment of Tribal Advisory Councils, and the President's power to make regulations. The Governor has the authority to modify or exempt laws in these areas. This schedule is crucial for the welfare and protection of Scheduled Tribes, ensuring their distinct identity and rights are preserved while integrating them into the mainstream.

question: 'Uniform Civil Code' is mentioned in which of the following? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Fundamental Rights
Directive Principles of State Policy
Preamble
Fundamental Duties
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Directive Principles of State Policy

Explanation:
The Uniform Civil Code is mentioned in Article 44 of the Indian Constitution, which falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy. This article directs the state to endeavor to secure a uniform civil code for all citizens throughout India. The Directive Principles are contained in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution. These principles are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country. The Uniform Civil Code aims to replace personal laws based on religious customs with a common set of laws governing every citizen. It is not included in Fundamental Rights, the Preamble, or the Fundamental Duties.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which Article mentions Uniform Civil Code? → Article 44
☛ Which Part of Constitution contains Uniform Civil Code? → Part IV
☛ Which Article directs state to secure Uniform Civil Code? → Article 44
☛ Is Uniform Civil Code justiciable? → No, it is a Directive Principle
☛ What is the aim of Uniform Civil Code? → Uniform personal laws for all citizens
question_hi: 'समान नागरिक संहिता' का उल्लेख निम्नलिखित में से किसमें है? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: मौलिक अधिकार
राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व
प्रस्तावना
मौलिक कर्तव्य
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में समान नागरिक संहिता का उल्लेख अनुच्छेद 44 में किया गया है, जो राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों के अंतर्गत आता है। यह अनुच्छेद राज्य को निर्देश देता है कि वह पूरे भारत में नागरिकों के लिए एक समान नागरिक संहिता सुनिश्चित करने का प्रयास करे। राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व संविधान के भाग IV (अनुच्छेद 36-51) में शामिल हैं। ये तत्व न्यायोचित नहीं हैं, अर्थात इन्हें अदालतों में लागू नहीं किया जा सकता, लेकिन ये देश के शासन में मौलिक हैं। समान नागरिक संहिता का उद्देश्य विभिन्न धार्मिक समुदायों के लिए व्यक्तिगत कानूनों को बदलकर एक सामान्य कानून बनाना है। यह मौलिक अधिकारों, प्रस्तावना या मौलिक कर्तव्यों में शामिल नहीं है।

question: Who was elected the first President of the country after independence on 26 January 1950? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 3)

Explanation:

He also served as the Chairman of the Constituent Assembly and held the presidential office from 1950 to 1962. During his tenure, India strengthened its democratic system.

question: Which of the following are the grounds for the removal of a judge of a High Court or the Supreme Court? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Proved incapacity and lack of qualifications
Proved misbehaviour and incapacity
Proved misbehaviour and criminal conviction
Proved misbehaviour and administrative errors
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Proved misbehaviour and incapacity

Explanation:
According to Article 124(4) and 217(1)(b) of the Indian Constitution, a judge of the Supreme Court or High Court can be removed only on the grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. The removal process requires an impeachment motion passed by a special majority in both houses of Parliament. The term 'proved' means that the misbehaviour or incapacity must be established after an inquiry. Lack of qualifications or criminal conviction are not constitutional grounds for removal. This provision ensures the independence of the judiciary. To date, no judge has been removed through this process.

☛ Grounds for removal → Proved misbehaviour and proved incapacity
☛ Required majority → Special majority in both houses (2/3 of present and voting)
☛ Any judge removed so far? → None
☛ Procedure name → Impeachment
question_hi: उच्च न्यायालय या सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश को हटाने के क्या आधार हैं? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: सिद्ध अक्षमता और योग्यता की कमी
सिद्ध दुर्व्यवहार और अक्षमता
सिद्ध दुर्व्यवहार और आपराधिक दोषसिद्धि
सिद्ध दुर्व्यवहार और प्रशासनिक त्रुटियां
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है सिद्ध दुर्व्यवहार और अक्षमता

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 124(4) और 217(1)(b) के अनुसार, उच्चतम न्यायालय या उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश को केवल सिद्ध दुर्व्यवहार या अक्षमता के आधार पर हटाया जा सकता है। हटाने की प्रक्रिया के लिए संसद के दोनों सदनों में विशेष बहुमत से महाभियोग प्रस्ताव पारित करना आवश्यक है। 'सिद्ध' शब्द का अर्थ है कि दुर्व्यवहार या अक्षमता को जांच के बाद साबित किया जाना चाहिए। योग्यता की कमी या आपराधिक दोषसिद्धि को संविधान में हटाने का आधार नहीं बनाया गया है। यह प्रावधान न्यायपालिका की स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए बनाया गया है। अब तक किसी भी न्यायाधीश को इस प्रक्रिया से नहीं हटाया गया है।

question: By which of the following Amendment Acts was Article 21(A) inserted in the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: 44th Amendment Act
73rd Amendment Act
42nd Amendment Act
86th Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 86th Amendment Act

Explanation:
Article 21(A) was inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002. This article provides free and compulsory education as a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years. The amendment added Article 21(A) after the original Article 21 and also modified Article 45 and inserted Article 51A(k). The Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009 was enacted under this article to enforce it.

☛ Which article was added by 86th Amendment regarding parental duty? → Article 51A(k)

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान में अनुच्छेद 21(A) किस संशोधन अधिनियम द्वारा जोड़ा गया था? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)

अनुच्छेद 21(A) को 86वें संशोधन अधिनियम, 2002 द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। यह अनुच्छेद 6 से 14 वर्ष के बच्चों के लिए शिक्षा के मौलिक अधिकार के रूप में मुफ्त और अनिवार्य शिक्षा प्रदान करता है। इस संशोधन ने मूल अनुच्छेद 21 के बाद 21(A) डाला और अनुच्छेद 45 व 51A(k) में भी बदलाव किया। भारत में शिक्षा का अधिकार (RTE) अधिनियम 2009 इसी अनुच्छेद के तहत लागू किया गया।

question: Which of the following Acts transferred the power from the British East India Company to the British Crown in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Government of India Act, 1858
Government of India Act, 1935
Indian Councils Act, 1909
Pitt's India Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1858

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred power from the East India Company to the British Crown, establishing direct British rule in India. Under this Act, the Governor-General of India was given the title of 'Viceroy'. Lord Canning became the first Viceroy. This Act was passed after the Revolt of 1857 and brought Indian princely states under the sovereignty of the British Crown. It also abolished the Board of Control and the Court of Directors.

question: Which of the following is NOT a correct classification of the Directive Principles of State Policy? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Principles for the International Peace and Security
The economic and social principles
The Nehru Principles
The Gandhian Principles
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Nehru Principles

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy in Part 4 of the Indian Constitution are classified into three categories: Socialistic Principles (economic and social), Gandhian Principles, and Liberal-Intellectual Principles (including international peace and security). 'The Nehru Principles' is not an official classification; it is a misleading term. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described these principles as non-justiciable, yet they are fundamental in governance. These principles aim to establish a welfare state and are inspired by the Irish Constitution.

question: The principles of social justice incorporated in the Directive Principles are influenced by which philosophy? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Capitalism
Anarchism
Gandhism
Communism
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gandhism

Explanation:
The principles of social justice in the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) of the Indian Constitution are primarily influenced by Gandhian philosophy. Gandhi's ideas emphasized gram swaraj (village self-governance), dignity of labour, and equitable distribution of resources. Provisions like Article 40 (village panchayats), Article 43 (living wage and decent standard of life), and Article 47 (prohibition of intoxicating drinks) reflect Gandhian ideology. Unlike communism or capitalism, Gandhism advocates a middle path focused on economic equality and social justice. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described the Directive Principles as the economic democracy of the nation.

question: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act added the Right to Education in the Constitution, under which Article? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 21 A
Article 19
Article 20
Article 22
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 21 A

Explanation:
The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added the Right to Education as Article 21A in the Indian Constitution. This amendment inserted a new Article 21A after Article 21, providing free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years. It was made a Fundamental Right. Additionally, Article 45 (Directive Principle) was amended to emphasize early childhood care and education, and Article 51A(k) was added as a fundamental duty of parents to provide educational opportunities to their children. This amendment forms the constitutional basis for the National Education Policy 2020 and the RTE Act 2009.

question: What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha as per the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: 200
225
250
238
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 250

Explanation:
As per Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250. Out of these, 12 members are nominated by the President from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service. The remaining 238 members are indirectly elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union Territories. Currently, the Rajya Sabha has 245 members, including 229 representing states, 4 representing Union Territories, and 12 nominated members. This is less than the maximum limit prescribed by the Constitution.

question: Social or Collective Ownership, Central Planning Authority and Social Welfare are the features of which type of economy? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Capitalism
Socialism
Imperialism
Communism
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Socialism

Explanation:
A socialist economy is characterized by social or collective ownership of the means of production. Resource allocation is done by a central planning authority, usually under government control. The primary objective is social welfare rather than profit maximization. Socialism ensures equitable distribution of income and the government runs welfare schemes like health and education. Unlike capitalism, which prioritizes individual profit, socialism focuses on collective well-being. Communism also involves collective ownership but aims for a classless society and the eventual withering away of the state, whereas socialism retains the state as a key player in planning and welfare.

☛ Who owns resources in a socialist economy? → Social or collective ownership
☛ Who allocates resources in socialism? → Central planning authority
☛ What is the main goal of socialism? → Social welfare
☛ Key difference between capitalism and socialism? → Capitalism: individual profit; Socialism: collective good
☛ Which schemes are common in socialism? → Health, education, and welfare schemes

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution explicitly prohibits the State from making any law that violates Fundamental Rights? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 42
Article 30
Article 13
Article 32
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 13

Explanation:
Article 13 of the Indian Constitution explicitly prohibits the State from making any law that violates Fundamental Rights (Part III). Article 32 provides remedies for enforcement of Fundamental Rights, Article 30 grants minorities the right to establish educational institutions, and Article 42 directs the State to ensure just and humane working conditions.

question: The 7th Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution, 1956, primarily dealt with the reorganisation of states based on what criteria? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Economic basis
Geographical basis
Linguistic basis
Cultural basis
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Linguistic basis

Explanation:
The 7th Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution, 1956, primarily dealt with the reorganisation of states based on a linguistic basis. This amendment was enacted following the recommendations of the States Reorganisation Commission (1953-55), chaired by Justice Fazal Ali. The commission considered language as the primary criterion for state formation, leading to the creation of Andhra Pradesh (1956) as the first state formed on linguistic lines. The 7th Amendment redefined state boundaries and introduced the concept of Union Territories. It abolished the classification of states into Parts A, B, C, and D, thus simplifying the administrative structure. Hence, the reorganisation was based on linguistic and administrative considerations.

question: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)

Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Union Public Service Commission
National Green Tribunal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Green Tribunal

Explanation:
The National Green Tribunal (NGT) is a statutory body, not a constitutional body. Constitutional bodies are those that are directly mentioned in the Constitution of India. The Election Commission of India (Article 324), the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (Article 148), and the Union Public Service Commission (Article 315) are constitutional bodies established by the Constitution. The NGT was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, an act of Parliament, not under the Constitution. It was created for the speedy disposal of environment-related cases.

question: Which Schedule of the Constitution of India deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to states and union territories? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Eighth Schedule
Fourth Schedule
Seventh Schedule
Sixth Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fourth Schedule

Explanation:
The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution of India deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to states and union territories. It specifies the number of seats each state and union territory is entitled to, based on their population. The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of Parliament, with a maximum strength of 250 members. Currently, it has 245 members, out of which 233 represent states and union territories, and 12 are nominated by the President. The allocation of seats in the Fourth Schedule ensures proportional representation of states based on population, thereby maintaining balance in the federal structure.

question: The 95th Amendment Act of 2009 extended the reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for which categories of citizens? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Other Backward Classes (OBC)
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (SC/ST)
Minorities
Women
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (SC/ST)

Explanation:
The 95th Amendment Act of 2009 extended the reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) for a further period of ten years, from 2010 to 2020. Originally, this reservation was intended for 70 years (1950-2020), but was earlier extended by the 79th Amendment in 1999. This constitutional amendment is governed by Article 330 (for Lok Sabha) and Article 332 (for State Assemblies). The purpose is to ensure adequate political representation for SC/ST communities. The 95th Amendment continued the reservation that was set to expire in 2010.

question: What was the Supreme Court's ruling regarding the Lieutenant Governor's (LGs) powers in Delhi, as per the judgement given by the three-judge bench led by Chief Justice DY Chandrachud, in August 2024? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)

question: According to the Indian Constitution, which of the following is NOT the function of the Union Public Service Commission? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 2)

To advise on disciplinary matters affecting government servants
To advise on selection for the posts of high diplomatic nature
To advise on claims of legal proceedings instituted against a government servant
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To advise on selection for the posts of high diplomatic nature

Explanation:
Under Article 320 of the Indian Constitution, the functions of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) are defined. UPSC's primary role is to advise on the suitability of candidates for appointment, promotion, and transfer. It also advises on disciplinary matters affecting government servants, such as disciplinary proceedings. Additionally, UPSC advises on claims related to legal proceedings instituted against a government servant. However, advising on selection for posts of high diplomatic nature is not a function of UPSC. Such posts are selected directly by the President without consulting UPSC. Hence, this option is not part of UPSC's functions.

question: Article 39 of the Constitution directs the State to secure which of the following? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Right to privacy
State to secure a social order
Right to work
Equal pay for equal work
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Equal pay for equal work

Explanation:
Article 39 is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) of the Indian Constitution. It directs the State to secure certain socio-economic justice for citizens. Specifically, Article 39(d) states that the State shall ensure that both men and women receive equal pay for equal work. This provision promotes gender equality and prevents discrimination in the workplace. Other options such as the right to privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21, not a directive principle. Securing a social order is outlined in Article 38. The right to work is included in Article 41, but it is not part of Article 39. Therefore, the correct answer is equal pay for equal work.

question_hi: संविधान का अनुच्छेद 39 राज्य को निम्नलिखित में से किसकी सुरक्षा का निर्देश देता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: गोपनीयता का अधिकार
राज्य को एक सामाजिक व्यवस्था सुरक्षित करना
कार्य करने का अधिकार
समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 39 भारतीय संविधान के राज्य नीति निदेशक सिद्धांतों (भाग IV) का हिस्सा है। यह राज्य को नागरिकों के लिए कुछ सामाजिक-आर्थिक न्याय सुनिश्चित करने का निर्देश देता है। विशेष रूप से, अनुच्छेद 39(d) कहता है कि राज्य यह सुनिश्चित करेगा कि पुरुषों और महिलाओं को समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन मिले। यह प्रावधान लैंगिक समानता को बढ़ावा देता है और कार्यस्थल पर भेदभाव को रोकता है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे गोपनीयता का अधिकार अनुच्छेद 21 के तहत मौलिक अधिकार है, न कि निदेशक सिद्धांत। राज्य को एक सामाजिक व्यवस्था सुरक्षित करना अनुच्छेद 38 में उल्लिखित है। कार्य करने का अधिकार अनुच्छेद 41 में शामिल है, लेकिन यह अनुच्छेद 39 का हिस्सा नहीं है। इस प्रकार, सही उत्तर समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन है।

question: The provision for the establishment of an inter-state council to promote co-operative federalism is found under which Article of the Indian constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (05/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 270
Article 275
Article 256
Article 263
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 263

Explanation:
Article 263 of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of an Inter-State Council to promote cooperative federalism. This council facilitates coordination and resolution of disputes between the Centre and States or among States. The President can order the creation of such a council. Currently, the Inter-State Council Secretariat functions under this provision. Other options: Article 270 (distribution of taxes), Article 275 (grants-in-aid), and Article 256 (directions to States) are unrelated.
